Subject: Kickoff: model shortlist + token baseline for Nimbus integration

Hi Rachel / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Nimbus is excited to move into a scoped pilot. Before our technical kickoff next Wednesday, Procurement asked for a short write-up showing the model candidates you expect us to evaluate, the context length recommendations for our primary flows, and a first-pass monthly token estimate so we can size the committed capacity.

Quick background on our side: product search + description generation will be the primary feature (users will send product metadata + 1–2 recent session messages). We also plan a limited follow-up chat flow for returns/helpdesk where we will need 2–4 turns of context retained. Estimated MAUs for the pilot: ~25k, ramp to 40k if pilot metrics look good.

Can you provide a short shortlist (2–3 candidate models, tradeoffs), recommended context window per flow, and a simple token-per-session estimate we can send to Procurement? If you already have a template, a spreadsheet is fine.

Thanks — can you get something over by COB Tuesday PST?

Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Integrations, Nimbus Retail

Subject: Re: Kickoff: model shortlist + token baseline for Nimbus integration

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. 

Attached are two artifacts: a concise model shortlist and an initial token baseline CSV (nimbus-model-shortlist-v1.xlsx, initial-token-estimates.csv). Below is the one-page summary you can pass to Procurement; I’ll be on the kickoff and we’ll review these in detail.

One-page summary (for Procurement):
- Candidate models (quick tradeoffs):
  • Mosaic-13B-int8 (higher throughput, lower cost; good for structured product doc generation; slightly lower instruction-following vs larger dense models)
  • Redstar-8B-q4 (fast, lowest cost for high-concurrency read/complete scenarios; recommended for pure retrieval + short generation tasks)
  • LlamaX-30B-std (better for multi-turn conversational quality and longer, nuanced returns/helpdesk flows; higher cost/throughput footprint)

- Context window guidance (per flow):
  • Product search + quick description (primary): 2–3k token window recommended (product metadata + 1 message history + prompt).
  • Multi-turn returns/helpdesk: 6–8k window to keep 3–4 prior turns + order history snippets.
  • Long-batch summarization (nightly): can use 16k+ off-peak if needed (we can batch these to reduce cost).

- Baseline token estimate (pilot):
  • Pilot MAU: 25k users; expected sessions/month: ~35k (1.4 sessions/user/mo).
  • Average request composition (primary flow): 600 prompt tokens (metadata + user message) + 300 response tokens = 900 tokens/session.
  • Monthly pilot tokens ≈ 35k * 900 ≈ 31.5M tokens/month (generation + input).
  • Peak concurrency guidance: expect 200–400 concurrent requests during promo spikes; recommend Dedicated baseline with autoscale headroom or hosted with burst + fallback to cheaper variant.

Notes / cost levers:
- Prefix/KV cache on product metadata reduces prompt tokens substantially for repeat SKU lookups.
- Consider using Redstar-8B for read-heavy flows and LlamaX-30B reserved for escalation flows to control unit economics.
- We included a conservative reserve multiplier of 1.25 in the CSV for error/regen overhead.

Action items:
1) Review attached shortlist + token CSV and confirm Procurement wants a single monthly committed band or a two-tier pilot/scale schedule.
2) Confirm whether Nimbus needs audit logs retention >90 days (affects pricing).
3) Kickoff on Wednesday 11/4 at 10:00 PST — Ben/Monica/Tessa will join.

Attached: nimbus-model-shortlist-v1.xlsx, initial-token-estimates.csv

—
Rachel Kim
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@nimbusretail.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: model shortlist + token baseline for Nimbus integration

Quick note: agree with the above. Two operational suggestions to include in the kickoff discussion:

- Enable request coalescing/batching for product-detail generation where the client pulls multiple SKUs in a single call (saves ~30–50% tokens per user in some flows).
- Add prefix-cache TTL guidance per SKU (we recommend 24h for frequently updated catalogs; shorter for rapidly changing prices).

Also: for auditing — what retention window does Nimbus need for request logs? 90 days is default we show in the SOW; increasing to 365 days will change storage costs.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Alex
